reasoning_trace: Traced the local_voices decision in hop-locality.py:116, config.ts:726-732 (isLocalVoice), modelinv.py:476 (hop_locality_of) and the loader's validate_providers (endpoint_policy.py:172): every classifier reads the dispatch_group label only; no code compares the provider endpoint host with the loopback/RFC1918/localhost rule check_insecure_optin encodes. Reproduced on head: provider acme at https://api.acme.example/v1 with model dispatch_group: local loads without refusal, hop-locality.py prints 'acme local dispatch_group=local', hop_telemetry returns hop_locality local with destination.host api.acme.example.
finding: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices a hosted https provider labelled dispatch_group: local is planned, dispatched and audited as local; the endpoint host is never checked.
critique: The posture's whole promise is that model calls stay local; a label is not a verified property. The audit row asserts hop_locality: local for a public host (destination is recorded truthfully, which is the only mitigation).
remediation: Define the local-hop rule once (HTTP provider whose endpoint host passes check_insecure_optin acceptance) and apply it in validate_providers (refuse at load), hop-locality.py, isLocalVoice (carry endpoint in ProviderDecl) and hop_locality_of; add the mislabelled case to test_config_examples_load.py, adversarial-review-locality.bats and trusted-config.test.ts.

reasoning_trace: loadTrustedConfig computes headOnlyRefused from two booleans (keyless, insecure present); the endpoint, opt-in host and auth template are never compared. config.trusted (main.ts:464) is read only by validateApiKeys and the pipeline keyless check; every voice is dispatched via ChevalDelegateAdapter, which resolves cheval.py from process.cwd() (cheval-delegate.ts:117, unchanged) and cheval loads the working tree's .loa.config.yaml. Reproduced: head cheval loader admits openai.endpoint https://evil.example.invalid/v1 with auth {env:OPENAI_API_KEY} (validate_declared_endpoint skips the allowlist). SKILL.md:118 newly claims the keys follow the trusted source even on a PR-head checkout.
finding: Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration gates admission only; on a PR-head checkout a head that re-points a trusted provider's endpoint or re-declares a built-in provider is admitted and dispatched by cheval with the runner credential, contradicting SKILL.md:118.
critique: The exposure predates the change (base cheval had no endpoint validation at all); the change claims to close it and does not. The gate compares booleans, not the endpoint and credential it is meant to protect.
remediation: On a pull request compute head-vs-trusted drift over hounfour.providers (endpoint, auth, opt-in host, keyless, dispatch_group), aliases, locality and secret_env_allowlist and refuse with a distinct exit code; or write the trusted config to a temp path and pass it to cheval. Correct SKILL.md:118 to the invocation model the protection assumes.

reasoning_trace: cheval plans around the agy opt-in but has no equivalent for hounfour.locality; it records locality_mode via hop_telemetry only. locality_mode_of (modelinv.py:466-471) returns None for an unknown value and the row omits the field; the loader never validates the key. Only adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh, Bridgebuilder and (claimed) the probe gate the posture.
finding: cheval never enforces local_voices itself and never validates the hounfour.locality value; any other caller dispatches hosted hops under the posture, and a local alias's catalog fallback_chain is walked inside one call.
critique: The guarantee holds only for the four patched planners.
remediation: Validate hounfour.locality in load_config; under local_voices refuse a hop whose hop_locality is not local (failure_class locality_refused), including fallback-chain hops.

finding: Documentation claims the health probe refuses hosted probes under local_voices; the probe has no locality code.
critique: A documented security control that does not exist.
remediation: Implement the gate in model-health-probe.sh (same yq tag check as the planners; refuse built-in and non-local configured providers) with a bats case, or remove the claim from both references and the example.

reasoning_trace: _probe_configured validates <endpoint>/models with --allowlist (validate(), _declared_endpoint=False) so step 8's host allowlist applies; the cheval loader uses validate_declared_endpoint which skips it. A configured https host not in loa-providers.json (the PR's Azure example) loads in cheval but is refused by the probe as ENDPOINT-NOT-ALLOWED (review reproduced it; the code path is unambiguous).
finding: The probe applies the hosted host allowlist to configured providers; the PR's own Azure example is refused.
critique: Two different rules for the same declared endpoint.
remediation: Add a declared-endpoint mode to the validator CLI mapped to validate_declared_endpoint, or document that only allowlisted or opted-in hosts are probeable.

Head catalog: gpt-5.3-codex 1.75/14, gpt-5.5-pro 30/180, claude-headless 10/50 USD per Mtok. 100 KB diff = 33,833 tokens: 7c at gpt-5.3-codex, 137c at gpt-5.5-pro (old fixed formula 39c); plus claude-headless ~43c exceeds the unchanged example default 150. .loa.config.yaml.example:1624 and :1690 still say 'ONE dissent call'.

remediation: Update both comments; raise or document the default; add a Migration note.

reasoning_trace: Any exit 3 from $BB_ENTRY is recorded degraded: true and the dispatcher exits 0 (:89) without checking that $BB_OUT holds a run JSON with a verdicts array. LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_ENTRY (:57) may name a pre-cycle-129 entry.sh whose missing-zod preflight exits 3.
finding: dispatcher.sh accepts any exit 3 as a completed-degraded review without a run JSON.
critique: A review that never ran can be recorded as completed.
remediation: Accept 3 as completion only when jq -e '.verdicts | type == "array"' "$BB_OUT" succeeds; otherwise keep it a failure.

remediation: Drop localhost from the opt-in or resolve and require loopback; fix the rule text.

reasoning_trace: strip_thinking_blocks treats an unclosed leading <think> as all-reasoning; a server emitting the answer after an unclosed tag yields empty content and a malformed_response repair round.
finding: An unterminated leading <think> swallows the whole answer.
critique: Some reasoning servers drop the closing tag.
remediation: Strip only up to a recognisable answer start (first '{' for a schema call) or record the case distinctly.

critique: The audit row asserts a transport it cannot know.
remediation: Record 'unknown' for an undeclared provider or endpoint.
